formats.key: Permit(address owner,address spender,uint256 value,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline)
effects: Sets the allowance of `spender` over the owner's Arbitrum WBTC to exactly `value`. This replaces any earlier allowance (ERC20PermitUpgradeable.permit → _approve(owner, spender, value)).
Uses up the owner's current permit nonce, so any other pending permit signed with that nonce stops working.
The signature is valid only until `deadline` (require(block.timestamp <= deadline)). Anyone who holds the signature can submit it.
formats.shown: "Authorize spending of tokens", with the spender as a raw address, the maximum amount in WBTC ("Unlimited" at 2^255 or more), the valid-until date and the owner.

findings.title: Permit test covers only a finite amount; the 'Unlimited' threshold rendering is never exercised.
findings.evidence: cases/0.json message.value "25000000" renders "0.25 WBTC"; descriptor field value has threshold "0x8000…" and message "Unlimited", but no case sends a value at or above 2^255.
findings.fix: Add a test case with value = type(uint256).max and expect "Unlimited" for 'Max spending amount'.
